The paper is primarily made of wood pulp, a fact that Arthur, a man who treats every minor inconvenience as a personal affront to his dignity, was currently reciting to his wife, Linda, in a tone usually reserved for explaining tax law.

"Wood pulp," Arthur repeated, tapping the dashboard of their minivan. "Cellulose fibers. Bound together with lignin. Much like this marriage, if we’re being honest."

Linda didn’t look up from her phone. "Arthur, please. We’re on a family road trip. The kids are in the back. Try to be whimsical."

"Whimsy is not a structural integrity standard, Linda."

As if on cue, the GPS screen flickered. The usual calm, robotic voice of the navigation system vanished, replaced by a voice that sounded suspiciously like a late-night game show host with too much caffeine in his system.

*"Welcome back, travelers! You’re currently driving at a speed that suggests you’re either late or deeply committed to mediocrity!"* the GPS boomed. *"But don’t worry! We’ve got a special bonus round for you! Would you like to take the next exit for a fabulous mystery destination?"*

Arthur slammed on the brakes. The car skidded slightly on the gravel shoulder. "Did you hear that? It’s malfunctioning. This is a safety hazard. I’m calling the manufacturer."

"Wait!" Linda’s eyes lit up. "It said 'fabulous mystery destination.' Remember that time we took the wrong turn in Vermont and found that pie shop? The one with the giant wheel?"

"That was a tragedy of navigation, Linda. Not a feature."

*"The clock is ticking, folks!"* the GPS shouted. *"Exit 42! Or keep driving into the abyss of boredom! Your choice, but I’m betting on chaos!"*

In the backseat, their ten-year-old son, Timmy, leaned forward. "Can we go? Please? I want to see what happens."

Arthur looked at Linda. Linda looked at Arthur. Arthur looked at the GPS, which was now displaying a spinning question mark.

"If we go," Arthur said, his voice tight, "I am holding you responsible for any deviation from the planned itinerary. We are going to the Grand Canyon. Not a 'mystery destination.'"

*"Ooh, spicy!"* the GPS cheered. *"Let’s roll!"*
